[ left to right ] || Text: LONDON 1996-08-30 || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: West Indian all-rounder Phil Simmons took four for 38 on Friday as Leicestershire beat Somerset by an innings and 39 runs in two days to take over at the head of the county championship. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: Their stay on top, though, may be short-lived as title rivals Essex, Derbyshire and Surrey all closed in on victory while Kent made up for lost time in their rain-affected match against Nottinghamshire. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: After bowling Somerset out for 83 on the opening morning at Grace Road, Leicestershire extended their first innings by 94 runs before being bowled out for 296 with England discard Andy Caddick taking three for 83. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: Trailing by 213, Somerset got a solid start to their second innings before Simmons stepped in to bundle them out for 174. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: Essex, however, look certain to regain their top spot after Nasser Hussain and Peter Such gave them a firm grip on their match against Yorkshire at Headingley. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: Hussain, considered surplus to England's one-day requirements, struck 158, his first championship century of the season, as Essex reached 372 and took a first innings lead of 82. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: By the close Yorkshire had turned that into a 37-run advantage but off-spinner Such had scuttled their hopes, taking four for 24 in 48 balls and leaving them hanging on 119 for five and praying for rain. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: At the Oval, Surrey captain Chris Lewis, another man dumped by England, continued to silence his critics as he followed his four for 45 on Thursday with 80 not out on Friday in the match against Warwickshire. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: He was well backed by England hopeful Mark Butcher who made 70 as Surrey closed on 429 for seven, a lead of 234. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: Derbyshire kept up the hunt for their first championship title since 1936 by reducing Worcestershire to 133 for five in their second innings, still 100 runs away from avoiding an innings defeat. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: Australian Tom Moody took six for 82 but Chris Adams, 123, and Tim O'Gorman, 109, took Derbyshire to 471 and a first innings lead of 233. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: After the frustration of seeing the opening day of their match badly affected by the weather, Kent stepped up a gear to dismiss Nottinghamshire for 214. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: They were held up by a gritty 84 from Paul Johnson but ex-England fast bowler Martin McCague took four for 55. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: By stumps Kent had reached 108 for three. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: Andre Agassi escaped disaster on Thursday but Wimbledon finalist MaliVai Washington and Marcelo Rios were not so fortunate on a night of upsets at the U.S. Open. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: The 11th-seeded Washington fell short of reprising his Wimbledon miracle comeback as he lost to red-hot wildcard Alex O'Brien 6-3 6-4 5-7 3-6 6-3 in a two hour 51 minute struggle on the Stadium court. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: Next door on the grandstand, 10th seed Rios lost to another player with a Wimbledon connection -- bad boy Jeff Tarango. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: The day programme went smoothly although sixth-seeded former champion Agassi had to wriggle out of a dangerous 3-6 0-4 hole, winning 18 of the last 19 games against India's Leander Paes. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: But the night belonged to the upstarts. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: Washington, who climbed back from a 1-5 deficit, two sets down in the third set against Todd Martin in the Wimbledon semifinals, looked poised for another sensational comeback. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: O'Brien, a winner two weeks ago in New Haven for his first pro title, served for the match at 5-4 in the third set before Washington came charging back. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: "I just kept saying to myself,' keep giving yourself the best chance to win, keep battling, maybe something will happen,'" said the 26-year-old O'Brien, ranked 65th. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: "I kept my composure and I was proud of myself for that -- usually I would have folded up the tent and gone home." || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: The hard-serving O'Brien, a former U.S. collegiate national champion, fired up 17 aces to ultimately subdue the never-say-die Washington. || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: The Texan blasted in two aces to hold serve at 5-2 and then converted his eighth match point for victory when Washington found the net with another backhand from 40-0. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: "You just kind of keep fighting and you keep trying to make him play a little bit. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: I think he got a little tight at a couple of moments, "said Washington." || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: But I think he served pretty well when he had to. " || Extract the entities.

[ left to right ] || Text: Tarango, whose Wimbledon tantrum two years ago brought him a $28,000 fine and suspension from this year's tournament at the All-England Club, argued calls and taunted fans in his lively two hour, 24 minute tango with Rios on the grandstand. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: A boisterous cheering section backed the distracted Chilean and booed the lanky American, who ate up all the attention. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: "I'm an emotional player," said the 104th-ranked Tarango. " || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: I think I played very well tonight, very focused. " || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: The match turned on the third-set tiebreaker, which the American won 7-5 much to the dismay of the spectators. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: "I love the crowd if they boo me every day. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: It fires me up, makes me play my best tennis, "Tarango said. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: "I played some of my best tennis in college when fraternities were throwing beer on me. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: If tennis was like that every day, I think everybody wold be having a lot more fun. " || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: Rios did not appreciate Tarango's antics. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: "He's always complaining too much," said Rios. " || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: But I think it's not that. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: I think I played really bad. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: It was tough to play at night. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: Balls were going really fast. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: I lost too many points that I never lose. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: I didn't play my tennis. " || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: "I don't see the ball like I see during the day. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: I play an American so that's why I play at night. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: I didn't feel good on the court. " || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: At the end of the match, Tarango blew sarcastic kisses to the crowd, then jiggled his body to a Rios rooting section in a jeering salute. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: "I support their enthusiasm," Tarango said about the fans. " || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: At the same time, they're cheering blatantly against me. || Extract the entities.
[ left to right ] || Text: After I won I figured I could give them a little razzle-dazzle. " || Extract the entities.
